title: Caught Playing Palworld 2 Hours Before Football Training, BeauMDC's Parents Had His Console Turned Into Food He Then Had to Eat
subtitle: A little-known 'bio-conversion' confiscation service promises to turn any gadget into fully edible, non-toxic mass. One Palworld session put it to the test.
excerpt: Instead of the usual grounding, BeauMDC's parents opted for a startup that converts confiscated electronics into something you can actually eat.
author: By Danielle Ferreira
heroHTML:

bodyHTML:
Most parents confiscate the console. BeauMDC's parents had his confiscated, converted, and served. After catching their son sneaking in a Palworld session a mere two hours before football training, they skipped the usual grounding and reached for something considerably stranger: a niche gadget called the ReMatter Home Unit, which claims to break down small electronics at a molecular level and reassemble the resulting mass into a soft, flavorless, fully digestible food block.

The ReMatter, marketed quietly to a small subset of "extremely online" parents as a novelty discipline tool, is not a large appliance — about the size of a microwave, with a single warning label reading "non-toxic conversion only; the manufacturer is not responsible for taste." BeauMDC's Switch went in intact. Forty minutes later, it came out as what his mother described as "basically a grey protein bar."

"He asked if he could at least keep his save file. I told him the save file was now also the bar."
— BeauMDC's mother, in a text message to relatives that has since gone semi-viral

BeauMDC, for his part, ate it. Teammates who heard about the ordeal before training said he showed up nine minutes late, visibly unbothered, and would only describe the taste as "like sadness and RGB lighting." Coaches confirmed he still made every drill.

A New Kind of Grounding

ReMatter's manufacturer declined to comment on individual households but confirmed the unit is "fully compliant with home food-safety conversion standards" and that the resulting mass, while edible, "is not intended to be enjoyable." Sales, a spokesperson admitted, have spiked noticeably since clips of the incident began circulating among parents of teenage gamers.

BeauMDC says he has already asked for a new Switch. His parents have not responded, though the ReMatter unit has reportedly been left sitting, ominously, on the kitchen counter.
